The Canada March 2027 pay stays on for the same impulse; the drift from 3.13 to 2.99 is a fade, not a regime change, and it is not a size-up.

rate-dove.thesis: Cash CORRA is 2.27 while the 2027 H-Z strip still averages about 3.23, so almost 96bp of 2027 catch-up tightening remains priced despite policy already being easy versus that forward path. Restrictive settings and growth weakness should prevent that hike-back from being delivered, which keeps the existing receive from 3.40 the right expression. Brent at 109.86 is the hawkish oil offset, not a reason to pay 2027 CORRA. Hold the 42.5 million H-Z average receive; do not collapse it into one contract or a bond.

rate-hawk.thesis: Cash SOFR at 3.89 versus September 2027 at 4.675 still sits well below the US 10-year at 5.09, so the 2027 terminal remains the underpriced higher-rate residual even after the mark from the 4.75 pay. Brent at 109.86 and euro inflation at a three-year high keep a goods-price impulse in the reaction function; that is even less in AONIA June 2027 at 4.81 versus cash 4.60 and still supports the CORRA March 2027 pay at 2.99 versus cash 2.27. The three existing pays already own that residual; do not add, cut, or rotate.

vol-convexity.invalidation: This hold is wrong if a later freeze shows a markable options structure with premium, implied vol, and strikes whose convex payoff rates and spot cannot express.
vol-convexity.thesis: VIX is 16.46 against Brent 109.86, euro inflation at a three-year high, the S&P near 7659, and policy strips above cash, with no listed options surface, strikes, or implied vols in the freeze. That is underpriced event convexity with uncertain timing, so spot and cash are the wrong instruments while equity vol stays contained. With the book flat and no markable convex payoff, standing aside dominates inventing a vol surface.
